deferred_source_units.source_text: The ways of the idle are strewn with thorns, but those of the courageous are well worn.
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual Proverbs 24:30-34 compares an unattended fool with a field or vineyard becoming wild and abandoned, followed by a warning about sleep and poverty. It does not describe thorns on the idle person's path or the contrasting well-worn way of the courageous. The broad neglect-and-overgrowth association is not retained as a sufficiently particular match.

target_units.text: A foolish man is like a cultivated field, and a person lacking understanding like a vineyard;
if you leave him alone, he will become wasteland, and grow wild with grass all over and become abandoned, and his stone fences are torn down.
Afterward I reconsidered; I looked so as to choose discipline.
“A little I doze, a little I sleep, a little I clasp my chest with my hands”—
but if you do this, your poverty will come marching in front, and your want like a good runner.
